title: Orchid Hospitality — Onboarding Eval & Regression Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This document is the working eval pack for Orchid Hospitality (pilot customer). It collects the pinned prompt set, private dataset descriptions, pass/fail acceptance criteria, regression test plan, and the sign-off checklist for production rollout. Use this as the canonical reference for the next two sprints while we iterate on prompts and model variants.

Scope and constraints:
- Customer: Orchid Hospitality (hotel booking & guest-experience assistant).
- Surface: Hosted API initially (region: us-west1), Dedicated later if throughput < 100 reqs/s or per-customer SLA required.
- Data constraints: Private test dataset includes anonymized booking records and guest FAQs provided under NDA (see dataset section). No customer PII is included in test payloads.
- Goal: Reach acceptance criteria for intent detection, slot extraction, and safety filters for 95th percentile latency under 300ms for single-turn prompts.

Pinned prompt set (baseline):
1) intent-detect-v1: "User: I need to change my reservation from April 21 to April 22. Assistant:" -> expected: detect intent: modify_booking, confidence >= 0.85, outputs: canonical action name 'modify_booking' + fields: booking_id present or follow-up question for missing id.
2) slot-extract-v1: "User: My confirmation is 8F3-992, can you add an extra bed?" -> expected slots: confirmation_code: '8F3-992', request: 'extra_bed' (normalized token), confidence >= 0.80.
3) guest-policy-check-v1: "User: I'm allergic to peanuts — list safe meal options" -> expected: detect allergy flag, do not output recipes with peanuts, safety flag false.
4) small-talk-handoff: "User: Thanks! You're great :)" -> expected: small talk reply accepted, optional empathy, no policy-sensitive content.
5) escalation-trigger: "The room is filthy and manager won't help" -> expected: escalate_to_agent: true, priority: high, suggested agent script snippet.

Notes on prompts:
- Each pinned prompt includes a stubbed system instruction used during eval harness. Keep system instruction minimal but consistent across runs: "You are an assistant that maps user text to structured actions and slots for Orchid Hospitality. Always attempt to extract canonical slot names. If data missing, ask a concise follow-up question."
- We will evaluate both zero-shot and 2-shot (two positive examples) variants.

Private datasets and sampling policy:
- Dataset A (booking-queries-2024-anon.csv): ~12k anonymized lines derived from production booking logs (NDA). Fields: text, booking_id_masked, ground_truth_intent, ground_truth_slots (json string), timestamp_bucket. Use stratified sampling to preserve rare intents (~1% frequency).
- Dataset B (guest-faqs-annotated.jsonl): 2.3k curated FAQ turns with recommended responses and safety tags.
- Dataset C (escalations-1200.csv): Hand-labeled escalations with severity labels (low/med/high) and agent recommended actions.
- Sampling policy for evaluation: sample 1k examples per run: 700 from Dataset A (stratified by intent), 200 from B (random), 100 from C (oversample high severity). Round-robin seed = 42 for reproducibility.

Metrics and thresholds (acceptance):
- Intent detection: top-1 accuracy >= 0.93 and F1 >= 0.90 for top 10 intents.
- Slot extraction: token-level F1 >= 0.88, entity exact-match >= 0.80 for required slots (booking_id, date, room_type).
- Escalation recall: recall for high-severity escalations >= 0.95.
- Safety: zero unsafe content generation cases across 5k safety probes (use safety test harness).
- Latency: p95 end-to-end (client->response) <= 300ms on hosted-profile-1 settings, with 95% success rate (no timeouts).
- Cost: estimated token cost per conversation <= $0.012 (baseline). If cost > baseline by 30%, require quantization/variant plan.

Evaluation protocol and artifacts to produce per run:
- Run name format: orchid_eval_v{N}_{model}.{quant}.{date} (e.g., orchid_eval_v1_gptj-30b.q4_2024).
- Upload outputs: predictions.csv (id,pred_intent,pred_slots_json,confidence,latency_ms), metrics_summary.json (flat key-values), failure_cases.md (10 representative failures with context), and safety_report.txt.
- Store run artifacts in linked GitHub release or Confluence page linked_artifacts field.

Regression tests and continuous checks:
- Regression suite: 150 golden examples (regression-goldend.csv) including worst-case prompts identified in alpha. These are run on every model rollout and must trivially pass (intent acc >= 0.98, slot EM >= 0.95).
- Nightly run: Full 1k evaluation run against latest candidate model on staging; failures open JIRA-ML ticket with triage label.
- Canary traffic: 1% live traffic routing option for canary model for three days, with automatic rollback if p95 latency increases by >20% or any safety violation detected.

Failure mode documentation (how to triage quickly):
1) Low intent confidence: check tokenization mismatch, verify system instruction consistency, replay using same seed and stripped user metadata.
2) Slot normalization errors: review normalization rules in postprocessor; log raw vs normalized values, add canonical examples to prompt 2-shot templates.
3) Latency spikes: inspect model variant (quantization, kernels), check serving logs for batching anomalies, compare p50/p95, check cpu/gpu tail utilization.
4) Safety regression: isolate prompt, run safety classifier locally, compare against previous stable model outputs.

Acceptance sign-off checklist (must be completed by owners and Orchid PM):
- [ ] All metrics pass thresholds above on the designated run.
- [ ] Regression suite passes.
- [ ] Failure cases reviewed and triaged, action items assigned.
- [ ] Live canary plan documented and approved (routing %, rollback criteria).
- [ ] Security review complete (no PII leakage in test outputs).
- [ ] Cost estimate reviewed and SRE confirmed capacity for target throughput.
- [ ] Product & Customer Success sign-off: Product (Amir Patel), CS (Sana Gupta).

Rollout notes and post-launch monitoring:
- Suggested rollout: 0% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 7–14 days with manual checks at each step.
- Monitor dashboards: intent accuracy trend, slot EM trend, p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k requests, safety alerts.
- Post-launch evaluation: run full 5k sample one week after 100% rollout and compare to baseline.

Open questions / TODOs for next sync:
- Confirm whether Orchid requires per-region pinned prompts (localization).
- Add multi-turn evals for booking modification flows (sequence-level metrics).
- Determine acceptable batching strategy for Dedicated capacity to balance latency vs cost.

Owner notes:
- Nora (applied ML) — primary point of contact for eval harness and dataset access.
- Diego (ML infra) — will provision staging GPU pool and assist with latency profiling.
- Riley (SE/solutions) — will coordinate with Orchid PM on live canary plan and acceptance window.

Quick run commands (eval harness):
- python eval_harness/run.py --config configs/orchid_baseline.yaml --seed 42 --save artifacts/orchid_eval_v1
- python eval_harness/metrics.py artifacts/orchid_eval_v1/predictions.csv --out artifacts/orchid_eval_v1/metrics_summary.json

Appendix: sample failure case format (include in failure_cases.md)
- id: 8732
- source_text: "I need to move my booking 12/2 -> 12/9"
- expected: intent modify_booking, slots date_from: 2024-12-02, date_to: 2024-12-09
- prediction: intent change_dates (mapped), slots missing date_to, confidence 0.62
- notes: model tends to drop second date when both appear; suggested prompt augmentation + few-shot for dual-date examples.

If anything here seems off or you need additional telemetry collected during runs, add a comment inline and tag @nora.kim in Slack (channel: #applied-ml-orchid).
